sipri.name: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database
sipri.basis: NATO-definition military spending, as compiled by SIPRI
sipri.note: SIPRI's own download. Includes paramilitary forces and military pensions where SIPRI could identify them; US$ at current prices and exchange rates. SIPRI marks some figures as its own estimates or as highly uncertain. File: SIPRI-Milex-data-1949-2025_v1.2.xlsx.

imf_gfs.name: IMF Government Finance Statistics: defence (COFOG GF02)
imf_gfs.basis: general-government spending on the defence function
imf_gfs.note: Country-reported government finance statistics. Narrower than SIPRI's definition (no paramilitary forces or military pensions in most countries). US$ figures convert the national-currency amount at the IMF's period-average exchange rate for the year.

eurostat_cofog.name: Eurostat government expenditure by function: defence (COFOG GF02)
eurostat_cofog.basis: general-government spending on the defence function, from national accounts
eurostat_cofog.note: Compiled by Eurostat from each member state's national accounts (EU members and a few others). US$ figures convert the national-currency amount at the IMF's period-average exchange rate (the ECB's for euro-area members).

ust_mts.name: US Treasury Monthly Treasury Statement: National Defense outlays
ust_mts.publisher: US Treasury (Bureau of the Fiscal Service)
ust_mts.basis: federal national-defense outlays, US fiscal year (October to September)
ust_mts.note: Budget function 050, federal government only (no state spending), year-to-date at the end of September. Includes Department of Energy nuclear weapons work and other defence-related outlays.

unavailable.name: NATO defence expenditure of NATO countries
unavailable.reason: Published as PDF reports only (def-exp-2025-en.pdf and earlier), with no machine-readable table or API, so it is not read here.

unavailable.name: IISS Military Balance+
unavailable.reason: A paid subscription database; there is no open download.

unavailable.name: National defence budgets of the UAE, Saudi Arabia, India and China
unavailable.reason: Not attempted country by country: these governments publish budgets as PDF statements, and none of them was found to offer a keyless machine-readable feed. The IMF's government-finance series above is the closest open, comparable record.

DJI.sipri: SIPRI publishes no figure for this country in the years compared.

ERI.sipri: Eritrea: Figures for Eritrea in 1995 include expenditure for demobilization. Eritrea has not publicly reported military expenditure figures since 2003.

CUB.sipri: Cuba: Figures for Cuba are for Defence & Internal Order. No figures for Cuba exist since 2018.

VEN.sipri: Venezuela: Due to sharp depreciation in the bolivar from 2014, the use of the official fixed exchange rate between bolivar and US$ is no longer possible. Thus alternative exchange rates have been used from 2013, this is a combination of DICOR, SICAD and DICOM (from 2014 onwards).

PRK.sipri: North Korea: The figures for North Korea are as reported by North Korean authorities. They do not include investment in the arms industry and R&D in dual-use technology, or various social welfare services provided through the military sector. Due to lack of economic data, no figures are provided for current US$, constant US$, spending as a share of GDP, per capita and as a share of government spending.

LAO.sipri: SIPRI publishes no figure for this country in the years compared.

TKM.sipri: Turkmenistan: The coverage of the series for Turkmenistan varies over time due to classification changes in the Turkmenistan system of public accounts. No information has been available since 1999.

UZB.sipri: Uzbekistan: The figures for Uzbekistan expressed in constant US dollars should be seen in the light of considerable difference between the official and the unofficial exchange rates. No military spending information has been available since 2003.

SYR.sipri: SIPRI publishes no figure for this country in the years compared.

ARE.sipri: United Arab Emirates: The military expenditure of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) is uncertain and lacking in transparency. Official documents and IMF reports sometimes give figures for defence spending, but only covering "goods and services" i.e. not salaries or military equipment. However, IMF reports gave figures for spending on "Abu Dhabi Federal Services" in 2014, said to be mostly for military spending.
ARE.note: SIPRI has published no UAE figure since 2014 (US$22755.1m), so the World Bank series, which republishes SIPRI, stops there too. For recent years the IMF figure is the only reading.

YEM.sipri: Yemen: The Republic of Yemen was formed in 1990 from the merger of the Yemen Arab Republic (North Yemen) and the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen (South Yemen).
